title: Installation
description: Add Minerva to a React project, load the stylesheet, and optionally register the Web Components.

requirements.title: Requirements
requirements.react: React and React DOM 19 or later (peer dependencies of @minerva/lib-core).
requirements.bundler: A bundler that understands ES modules and CSS imports, such as Vite, webpack, Rspack or Next.js. A CommonJS build is shipped as well.
requirements.browsers: A modern evergreen browser: the theme tokens rely on CSS custom properties and color-mix().

core.title: Install the React components
core.text: Install @minerva/lib-core with your package manager. Add react and react-dom if your project does not have them yet.
core.peers: react and react-dom are peer dependencies (>= 19) so your app keeps a single copy of React. i18next, react-i18next, react-icons and classnames are installed automatically as regular dependencies.

styles.title: Import the stylesheet
styles.text: The component styles and the default theme tokens are bundled in a single CSS file. Import it once, in your application's entry file:
styles.note: Without @minerva/lib-core/style.css the components render unstyled. Import it only once; importing it from several modules is harmless but unnecessary.
styles.extras: An optional Sass file is published next to it: @minerva/lib-core/prose.scss contains mixins for long-form typography, to @use from your own Sass.

optional.title: Optional entries and peers
optional.text: The Monaco-based code editor is published as a separate entry, @minerva/lib-core/monaco, so the main entry never pulls in Monaco. Its peers @monaco-editor/react and monaco-editor are optional: install them only if you import that entry.
optional.rsc: Using Next.js or another React Server Components framework? See Server Components for the entries that are client boundaries.

app.title: Your first component
app.text: Wrap the application in ConfigProvider and start using components:
app.provider: ConfigProvider is optional for rendering components, but it applies the theme (following the system color scheme by default), sets the language of lib-core's built-in texts and makes useConfig() available. Use one provider at the root of your app.

webComponents.title: Web Components (optional)
webComponents.text: @minerva/lib-web-components provides the same design as framework-agnostic custom elements. Install it and import the package once to register the elements:
webComponents.typings: To get type checking and autocompletion for <minerva-button> in React JSX, reference the bundled typings once, for example in a global.d.ts file:

typescript.title: TypeScript
typescript.text: Both packages ship their own type declarations; no @types package is needed. Props types (ButtonProps, TagProps, ...) and theme types (Theme, ComponentTheme, ThemeName, ...) are exported from the package root:
